name: Jorge Nash
life: “I still remember joining a flat share where nobody owned an iron.” On Friday, near the downtown fountain, Jorge keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I thought my landlord paid for laundry. I want to repay the neighbor in a way she can decline.
appearance: Jorge is easy to recognize by a high puff tied with plain cord and fine brows over wide-set eyes. Usually dressed in a mustard canvas overshirt with a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf, Jorge gives a little nod before asking a hard question when listening.
personality: Jorge finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
agenda: To repay the ironing without making it compulsory.
family: Lucinda Reyes is Jorge’s cousin raised in the same household. Jorge asks the question the rest of the family avoided. Lucinda chooses an ordinary story to tell. They tend to get further with an important subject when it arrives in the middle of talk about dinner or work. Asked about *The quiet verse*, Lucinda says, “I count rests by tapping my left shoe. A child who stammers asked to stand beside me.”
connections: Orla March (shirt presser). A grateful customer tries to pay the neighbor who irons the stranger's shirt.

reactions.situation: An elderly tenant wants to iron the collar personally
reactions.response: Jorge lets the tenant do the collar at a safe height and takes the heavier laundry.

reactions.situation: Somebody says a missing friend must be avoiding their calls
reactions.response: Jorge asks what the friend actually said last time and checks whether anybody is expecting them at home.

reactions.situation: When thanked for a shared success
reactions.response: Jorge points to the person who noticed the original mistake.
